# Multi-Level Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

> **Companion design document**. This is a companion document to
> [RFC-039 Compiler Architecture Refactoring](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md). It
> expands the RFC's phase sequence into **independently committable and independently verifiable**
> three-level tasks.
>
> The phase order and acceptance gates are governed solely by the body of RFC-039; this document
> only breaks the work down to executable granularity and records conflicts that have not yet been
> adjudicated.

## Positioning and Scope

| Level            | Count       | Meaning                                                                                               |
| ---------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **First level**  | 11 (P0–P10) | Phases, in one-to-one correspondence with RFC-039's phase sequence                                    |
| **Second level** | 73          | Task groups: work groups decomposed by phase, each of which can form and archive a team independently |
| **Third level**  | 263         | Work units that can be committed and verified independently                                           |

**Reserved numbering (not reused)**: P4 has no `4.7`/`4.8`, and P8 has no `8.1`; after the LALRPOP
route was withdrawn, `8.4` / `8.5` / `8.6` were also left unused (2026-11-25). All three have had no
corresponding entries since the WBS was established—the entire history of this document has zero
hits for the three headings `**4.7` / `**4.8` / `**8.1`
(`git log -S'**4.7' -- docs/src/dev/architecture/09-execution-wbs.md` can verify this), and there
are no references elsewhere in the repository. `8.1` corresponds exactly to phase 1 of `05` (test
resurrection and completion): that phase was split into P1 (`1.1`–`1.3`) and `8.8`, so P8's
numbering aligns with its phase numbers (phase 0 → `8.0`, phase 2 → `8.2`, and so forth).

**Covered by this document**: task decomposition, dependencies, parallel groupings, and binding of
acceptance criteria.

**Not covered by this document**: the design rationale for tasks (see `02`–`08`) or the
justification for phase ordering (see RFC-039).

**Registration convention (effective 2026-10-12)**: every newly registered second- or third-level
row **must contain two fields**—**Owning phase** (the P to which it actually belongs, which may
differ from the current section) and **Blocks mainline**; `pending scheduling` is no longer the
default status, and an unmarked row is treated as **not schedulable**. IDs must be unique throughout
the document (cross-track tasks use a track number, such as `029g.x`, and must not occupy an `N.x`
ID).

**Closure registration (effective 2026-11-24)**: checked rows contain only four items—the task ID,
status, **implementation commit short hash** (7 characters), and issue number (only when
applicable), written on one line:
`- [x] **3.24.1 Pattern-matching completion remainder** ✅ 4d608df3 (issue #405)`. **Do not record
the fix, criterion chain, gate thresholds, file line numbers, test names, or review conclusions**:
those belong in the commit message (`git show <short-hash>`). This table is a board, not a process
chronicle. **Do not record adjudication labels or restate conclusions**: “User adjudication A/B/C,”
“Option A,” “Final implementation is…” and similar text must not appear in this table—the board
answers only “complete or not”; consult the commit messages and RFC-039's decision registry for
adjudications and outcomes.

**Short hashes are authoritative after push**: closure rows contain the short hash on `origin/dev`
after the push. The order is **push the implementation commit first, then write the closure row**
(see “Commit hash is taken after push” in [commit-convention](../commit-convention.md)). The closure
commit itself carries no hash—self-reference is impossible.

**Count columns contain numbers only**: the first-, second-, and third-level counts under
`Positioning and Scope` contain only current values; increment/decrement history (`+1 = …`) does not
belong in the table.

## Current State: Gaps Found During Decomposition

While consolidating the “Implementation Points” of eight documents into this table, **five hard gaps
in the documentation system itself** were found. All have now been resolved:

| #   | Gap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Resolution                                                                                                                                 |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| G1  | **P5 has no implementation steps whatsoever**. RFC-039 defines P5 (checker splitting) and its acceptance criterion (C1 zero-diff), but none of the seven documents contains a section describing how to perform that split; the directory tree in `01-routing.md` contains one `annotations.rs` entry, the sole mention in the entire batch                                                                                                   | The P5 steps are supplied by this document (see below)                                                                                     |
| G2  | **The `include!` refactor has three ownership sites and zero implementations**. RFC-039 lists it under P4; `02` assigns the reference to itself; and `06` S7 also lists it. However, the change list in `02` (6 additions + 20 modifications) contains **no `semantic_tokens.rs`**                                                                                                                                                            | The implementation steps are assigned to §P5 5.1 here (after P4 is complete); references in RFC-039 and `06` now point here                |
| G3  | **Three concurrent lists of CI scripts**. `RFC` lists four `scripts/ci/*.py` scripts; `01` lists four scripts + one `cargo test`; `07` lists four different checks under different names; and `04` once listed `check-synth-boundary.py` (that script was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24). After deduplication, there are **at least nine new scripts but no canonical list**; `check-obligations.py` has dual ownership under P4 and P9 | See the unified list in §P9 of this document (10 active scripts, each owned by exactly one phase); all other documents refer to that table |
| G4  | **Conflict over the life or death of `precedence_inline.rs`**. `06` counts it among the “1005 lines to resurrect,” while B6 in the same document says it “must be deleted together with” the `Precedence` enum; `05` advocates deletion                                                                                                                                                                                                       | **Resurrect under P1 and retain under P8** (decision registry C1; Pratt is no longer to be removed)                                        |
| G5  | **Conflict in the wording of the L2 target**: RFC-039 and the directory index previously said “grammar-driven syntax”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Converged to a **declarative precedence table + an unambiguous language surface** ([05](05-frontend-paradigm.md) §Syntax); see P8 8.3      |

## Target Design: Phase Sequence

```
P0 仓库维护机制与代码放置规程 08 ← 新增，先立规矩
P1 复活孤儿测试并修缺陷 06 §S1
P2 建立等价性判据基线 07 全部
P3 修正确性漏洞（最小方案） 02 §S3-漏洞半部
P4 阶段契约与统一 Driver 02
P5 checker 文件内拆分 02 + 本文补齐
P6 类型表示单一化 03
P7 中间表示 SSA 化 04 } 可并行
P8 前端范式变更 05 }
P9 防反弹门禁（含统一脚本清单） 01 §防反弹 + 08 §可机检规则
P10 其余清理与状态修正 06 §S2/S3/S4/S5/S6
```

**Rationale for adding P0**: the three prohibitions (do not invent; do not pad endlessly; do not
patch when a refactor is required) constrain every action in P1–P10. The rules must be established
before implementation begins; otherwise, while resurrecting tests in P1, work would already begin
adding `mod` declarations to `tests/mod.rs`—precisely the cause of the G4 conflict.

### P3 Fix Correctness Defects (Minimal Approach)

Source: the defect-fix half of [02](02-stage-contract.md) §Implementation Points S3 + **the
2026-10-07 silent-drop-point audit (3.4)**

> **Semantic-correction routing (D59, adjudicated 2026-10-11)**: if this track or any subsequent
> phase discovers a defect where “the old behavior does not count as success”—**A silent failure / B
> silent mismatch / C undefined behavior and resource loss** (crash, stack exhaustion, or silently
> incorrect results)—it **may be fixed in passing during the refactor**, provided all four
> requirements are met: ① red before green (the red criterion must exist first and actually fail); ②
> the externally observable behavior of programs that “previously compiled and ran correctly” must
> not change (they must not begin failing, and their existing diagnostic codes / wording / exit
> codes must not be changed); ③ registration in the same commit (this row identifies the error
> type + a revision note for that phase + a required “Error type” line in the PR block); and ④
> baseline regeneration in the same commit + manual review of the diff. **The three categories D
> user-visible semantics / E external contract tables / F RFC-level design changes must still
> undergo adjudication. See [07 §Semantic-correction routing criteria](07-equivalence-oracle.md) for
> criterion details and the A–F allowlist; the approach of “default to a mega-refactor and register
> it afterward” is not accepted** (rationale: see RFC-039 D59: without a red criterion, a fix cannot
> be distinguished from a regression, conflicting with both “C5′ does not exist” and “no relaxation
> whatsoever”).

again**. **Risk**: the new E4018 on the multi-file path is a breaking change.

**3.4 acceptance**: 3.4.1 / 3.4.2 must have red criteria first (changing code first is prohibited);
3.4.3 requires manual review; 3.4.4–3.4.8 use C2/C3 and the 9.2 gate in P9 as the criterion.
**Risk**: the new diagnostic in 3.4.1 is a behavioral change and requires synchronized
corpus-differential baseline and CHANGELOG updates.

> **Stop-the-bleeding path**: P3 need not wait for all of P2. The only hard prerequisites for
> 3.1/3.2 are **2.3.2 (multi-file corpus layer) + 2.4.1/2.4.3 (two red criteria)**;
> 2.1/2.2/2.3.1/2.3.3 (the IR verifier, snapshots, single-file differential testing, and performance
> baseline) may proceed in parallel with P3. Stopping the bleeding from correctness defects such as
> `Sorted(3)` being silently accepted must not be blocked by snapshot infrastructure. 3.3
> (converting panics to diagnostics) has no prerequisite and may land at any time.

### External Track RFC-029g: Remove `pub` and Automatic Binding (External Track / #399 — Ordering Constraint D56)

Source: [RFC-029g](../../rfc/accepted/029g-remove-pub-and-auto-bind.md) (accepted 2026-10-02;
implementation not started), [#399](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/399). **This track
is not a design item of the refactor itself; it is a specification-compliance deletion forced by an
ordering constraint.** It is distinct from P10 S5 “lower the visibility of `pub` items” (narrowing
Rust `pub(crate)`).

**Why it must be completed wholesale before P4**: 029g's deletion surface overlaps with the rewrite
surfaces of all four refactoring phases. Reversing the order means repeating the same deletions and
baseline updates on the new grammar / checker layout / SSA IR.

| 029g deletion surface                                              | File                                                                                                               | Rewritten by which phase                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |

| AST `is_pub` ×2 (`Assign` / `TypeDefinition`)                      | `parser/ast.rs`                                                                                                    | **P6 6.5 AST dead variants** + P8 + D1 directory renaming (`parser/ast.rs` → top-level `src/ast/`)                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `auto_bind_to_type` and the pub branch of `collect_exports`        | `typecheck/checker.rs`, `environment.rs`                                                                           | **P5** (`include!` → true `mod` and checker splitting are **pure moves**, so the pub branch will be moved unchanged into the new files)                                                                                                                            |
| Dead-code exemption `exempt_pub` / `is_exported` and role dispatch | `typecheck/passes/dead_code.rs`, `module/orchestrator.rs` (inside `check_project`)                                 | **P4 4.2.2** (slimming down `check_project`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| The `Public` modifier in `semantic_tokens`                         | `typecheck/checker/semantic_tokens.rs`                                                                             | **P4 4.2.6** + P5 + 4.6 (D55)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `ir_gen`'s `is_pub`-ignoring binding                               | `middle/core/ir_gen.rs`                                                                                            | **P7** (`ir_gen.rs` SSA conversion)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| 31 occurrences of `pub` in `src/std/`                              | `std/list.yx` / `json.yx` / `option.yx` / `result.yx`                                                              | No phase changes them directly, but **P6's hard acceptance criterion requires zero differences in `src/std/` (`git diff --stat src/std/` is empty; direct-drive tests under `tests/` are excepted—see P6's hard acceptance section)**—they can only land before P6 |

**Side benefit**: 029g also deletes the dead `env.exports` table (populated in production with zero
repository-wide consumers) and the `is_exported`/`is_visible` accessors ⇒ one fewer “produced but
never consumed” field in P4's 4.3 obligation ledger.

**Acceptance (behavioral changes; red criterion first)**:

1. **Red before green**: each of the two behavioral changes must land a red criterion before code
   changes—① `pub` changes from “silently accepted” to a parse error; ② in Lib/Script roles,
   unreferenced top-level bindings newly report W1001 (pub items were previously always exempt).
2. **The test count must not decrease**: when deleting the `exempt_pub` cases and `is_pub` fixture
   in `typecheck/passes/tests/dead_code.rs`, they must be replaced by equivalent new cases.
3. **Baseline in the same commit**: diagnostic-set changes (the new parse error + new W1001) ⇒ the
   corpus-differential baseline (`tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl`) and CHANGELOG are updated in
   the same commit; the IR snapshot is expected to have zero diff, and any non-zero diff must be
   explained.
4. **Independent revert unit**: the entire batch occupies one commit group and must not be mixed
   with other phases (DoD 6).
5. `cargo test` / `clippy -D warnings` / `python scripts/rfc/check_tracking.py` are all green.

**Ordering**: it overlaps with 3.4 in files (`checker.rs`, `environment.rs`) ⇒ the two must be
serialized and must not run in parallel; **the whole track precedes P4** (RFC-039 D56). The 029g
track does not depend on 3.4; the implementer chooses which to start first based on available
context.

> **Commit cross-reference (2026-10-08)**: the incorporation of this section (P3.5 chapter +
> main-chain/constraint row) and RFC-039's D56 were merged in `97071c81b` while the workspace was
> being swept by the parallel-flow cleanup. The commit message records “3.4 supplement
> registration + documentation of the D57/D58 adjudications” and does not mention this track.
> History is not rewritten; following the existing convention (the `d5b18390` precedent, see the P2
> landing note), the change is registered in place as the basis for subsequent binary attribution.

The line-count change is an inevitable result of fixture entry and removal (after regenerating `corpus_probe`, it matches the checked-in baseline byte-for-byte) and **is not coverage loss**. **Known gaps (each named explicitly; old behavior = silently ignored or silently dropped; D60② should report but does not, category A)**: closure-value binding / block-body function declaration / named nested function declaration / built-in container constructors other than `len` with named arguments / whole-module import / RFC-004 binding arm. **Two of these are corrected based on P0 measurement**: ① **static-function forms** (both same-unit and cross-unit, definition-style and binding-style) are **entirely unavailable today**—same-unit `check` reports E3006; cross-unit definition-style `run` reports E6007; cross-unit binding-style `run` reports E6006; positional and named arguments produce the same code and are unrelated to named arguments, so this is not “named arguments being silently dropped”; ② **RFC-004 cross-unit positional arguments also fail** (`check` passes, `run` reports E6006); the root cause is that the dispatch name is absent from the merged function table, which is likewise unrelated to named arguments. **Fixed (4.9.10-S2b, D59 category A in-passing fix: old E6007/E1014 behavior was not success, so no previously successful program begins failing)**: ① **alias-import named arguments** (`use a.{Temp as X}` + `t.bump(k = 2.0)`); ② **namespace arm** (named arguments after `lib.Temp(..)`); ③ **inferred-receiver named arguments** (the receiver type is inferred and has no written annotation). These previously resulted in runtime E6007 with silently dropped arguments and check-time E1014 (`available: `) false rejections; all now bind by declaration-time formal name (value assertion 6.0; criterion `src/driver/tests/named_args_import_shapes.rs`, with the red state recorded in that file's header medical-history gate). Two identity-surface residuals remain, one of which has been closed: the unit's own same-named type + alias import (two same-named definition-side identities coexist and the import surface cannot register the unit's own declaration) **has been closed with the 4.9.10-S2a import-surface convergence** (the `same-name-type-local-and-alias-import` project fixture is fully green); **Hard constraint**: `collect_used_in_type` is used across modules by `inference/statements.rs:16`.
**If** the function is ever moved with the annotation family, `checker.rs` **must then** add
`pub(crate) use annotations::*;` so that this import remains unchanged; according to measurement,
5.3 **did not migrate it**, so this batch adds no re-export (the criterion was already satisfied).

**Only split confirmed large blocks.** Do not split modules of only 200–400 lines—this increases
navigation cost, reduces cohesion, and yields zero decoupling benefit. The remaining submodules
(signatures / type_defs / imports) await the files returning to 1,500 lines.

**6.9 Model and Invariants (First-Principles Rewrite, 2026-11-13)**

> **Model**: D62's end state is a **unified item world**—type positions and value positions share
> the same set of compile-time items. One strength declaration produces one quantifier reading
> `q ∈ {0,1,ω}`; `q` is the **sole input** to slot allocation, and the call-site actual view and
> implementation-header binding view are two projections of the same fact. Equality is a **pure
> determination** (the two sides are identical after normalization; it does not bind type
> variables); evidence is the **sole entry point** for `q=0` slots (four sources: literals / value
> environment / single-value pinning / Γ equality); erasure is the **runtime consequence** of `q=0`
> (both closed and open/recursive terms hold); Σ construction points **reuse** the same evidence
> interface rather than creating another set. **Completion criterion = the invariants hold, not that
> all subphase names have been checked off.**

> invariants holding.**

> **Partial order (not a serial chain)**: A facts → {A.C3, B.d, C.2, D design}; B core → {B.d, C.2,
> D implementation}; C.1 is independent and complete; F4 decision → A.C3; determination-point
> protocol → B.d; design review → D implementation. A.C3 and B.d may run in parallel but require
> file-surface coordination (C3 leans typecheck→mono, d leans types/solver→sema); C.2 may run in
> parallel with B.d after 6.9.2-B / 6.9.3a (does not depend on defeq); D implementation waits for
> confirmation of the B design package; it depends on A (q=0 erasure) and C.1 (dispatch), and may
> depend on the typed exit in 6.9.3. **P7 gate = the exits of A/B/C; D does not block.**

> **A.C3 prerequisite: F4 decision (adjudicated as A on 2026-11-16; measured)**: the old wording
> “`CheckOnly` evidence does not enter requests” is obsolete—`ConstEvidence`/`CheckOnly` have been
> deleted; the current mechanism is that open-term `normalize` returns `Unproven` ⇒ no request is
> created, and the representation layer `GenericArg::Const(ConstExpr)` can now hold `k-1`. **The
> decision is changed to two orthogonal decisions plus one terminating subdecision**: D-a
> representation (A: open terms enter `deferred` and are normalized before enqueueing / B: no
> specialization); D-b evaluation point (mono only; C-1's second field and C-2 reconstruction from
> IR both break the single representation / evaluator, so C-3 = A); **F4-T termination** (naive
> firing pushes the recursive chain into `max_depth` and triggers E3005; T-a: terminate at the
> instance's fold condition / T-b: bounded firing + return to the original at the boundary / T-c:
> termination layer or specification change). **Measure first, then adjudicate; before measurement,
> “A is already implementable” must not be treated as a conclusion.** **User (2026-11-16):
> D-a=A-closed, D-b=C-3, F4-T=T-b, bound=8; C3 implementation is a separate task, and the complete
> I4 form is not claimed.**

> **B.d prerequisite: determination-point protocol (not yet written)**: RFC-027 §12.1 specifies that
> “a determination point first follows the unified procedure; after unified failure, equivalence
> determination may be used, but all partial bindings produced by the unified attempt must first be
> rolled back.” The implementation must answer: is the entry point an outer wrapper around
> `solver.unify` or a new `decide` layer; may defeq be attempted only when both sides are ground
> (with no unbound variables); what are the snapshot/restore boundary and cost; do unify and defeq
> share one budget or have separate budgets. **Responsibility boundary**: unify remains responsible
> for subtyping / Any / Never; defeq determines equivalence only and does not take over subtyping;
> bidirectional subtyping must not be treated as equivalence (RFC-027 §12.1). **Provide the protocol
> and production call graph before writing code**; the 6.9.3c wiring contract wasted two rounds by
> assuming `can_assign` was the determination point, while `AssignmentChecker` has zero production
> instances.

> **E acceptance and residuals (I8, cross-cutting)**: every slice must provide ① zero
> corpus/IR-snapshot drift or an item-by-item classification; ② `testsuite run fast` + affected
> integration tests; ③ error-code generator idempotence (if an emission point / code table changes);
> and ④ classification of behavioral changes under D59 with red before green. **Wiring tasks
> additionally require**: production call-graph evidence (the production entry point, number of
> paths, and which are reachable); unit-test reachability must not be used to masquerade as user
> reachability; rollback and budget require measured numbers. **Residual disposition**: #537
> (category D, proof-function formal refinement silently dropped; do not fix before adjudication,
> and 6.9.4/6.9.5 must not depend on its fix), #539 (import-surface q=0; category-C boundary, and
> until closed 6.9.4 covers only module-local forms), #540 (deep-nesting stack overflow;
> **closed**—3.20.30 closed on 2026-11-14: a 64MB large-stack thread in the orchestration layer +
> parser depth gate MAX_PARSE_DEPTH=1024 + E0019; see the 3.20.30 row in 09), #541 (TailCall;
> **closed**—three locations entered and exited together on 2026-11-16: `call_form_is_rewritten` /
> `replace_calls_in_function` / `drop_erased_call_args` cover `Call`/`TailCall` through the
> single-point `rewritten_call_target`; init sections and function bodies share one rewrite site;
> red→green + three mutations), #542 (orphaned shared layer; **landed (2026-11-19)**: DCE pass + two
> post-mono entry-point wirings + C2c temporary avoidance removal; red→green, 402/402,
> function-table attribution and deviations), #552 (imported multi-parameter predicate proof
> execution; in the 6.9.5 neighborhood, separate case). **Ownership pending adjudication**: the four
> open-constraint tripwires (`Eq(N, n)`) in `rfc027_refined_transparency` do not belong to 6.9.4's
> constant-equality bridge; decide whether they remain in 6.9.4's outOfScope or move to 6.9.1 / the
> E4018 proof-function surface.

> **Non-claims / boundaries**: this item covers only record Σ (B: witness field), does not touch
> Π/`DepFn`, and does not claim the complete Π/Σ form; 6.9.4 covers only constant equality and does
> not fulfill the open-constraint `Eq(N,n)` tripwire; the second value position of `f(y)(y)` is

`git diff --stat tests/yaoxiang tests/baselines src/std/` must be empty **in every round of
6.1–6.7**. **Direct-drive test files** under `tests/` (tests that directly drive the changed code,
such as `tests/formatter_integration.rs`) may be changed when mechanically required, with each
change registered as **file / line count / reason**; **tests must not be deleted and assertions must
not be weakened**. **Exception**: 6.8.2 is a **behavioral-fix** batch (new diagnostic code +
baseline update), does not fall under this hard acceptance criterion, and is a separate round with
separate adjudication.

> **Revision relationship**: the original criteria (2026-10-26 decision ②) were written as
> `git diff --stat tests/ src/std/`, applying a blanket zero-diff requirement to all of `tests/`;
> the revised criteria **change only direct-drive test files from “zero diff” to “may be changed if
> file / line count / reason are registered”**, while the zero-diff requirement for the **corpus
> layer (`tests/yaoxiang`), baseline layer (`tests/baselines`), and standard library (`src/std/`)**
> remains unchanged. First application = 6.1.2: only `tests/formatter_integration.rs` changed, by

> the reason = the spelling change requires the expected type name in the assertion to be

**Risk**: the precedence table is the sole authority, and a missed consumer will **silently change
associativity** (no error, only a changed parse result). The defenses are the permanent D1–D3
assertions and the operator-property cross-check test; every new operator must enter both the table
and the cross-check test.

> **8.3–8.6 depend on `08`'s D0/D2**: if the grammar file is outside `parser/`, or action code
> refers back to `sema`, `check-boundary.py` will block it.

## Implementation Points: Dependencies and Parallelism

### Mandatory Serial Main Chain

`P0 → P1 → P2 → P3 → P3.5 → P4 → P5 → P6 → (P7 ∥ P8) → P9 → P10`

> **P3 stop-the-bleeding path (adjudicated 2026-10-05)**: P3's prerequisites are narrowed to
> **2.3.2 + 2.4.1 + 2.4.3** (multi-file corpus layer + two red criteria). The remainder of P2 (2.1
> IR verifier, 2.2 snapshots, 2.3.1/2.3.3 differential testing and performance baseline) may proceed
> in parallel with P3. Stopping the bleeding from correctness defects must not be blocked by
> criterion infrastructure; however, **P4 must still wait for all of P2**—the unified Driver
> requires all three layers of criteria to be in place.

| Constraint                | Reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| P0 → P1                   | The three prohibitions constrain every P1 action (1.2.x is precisely the act of adding `mod` declarations to `mod.rs`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| P1 → P2                   | Resurrecting tests changes the test count and corpus baseline                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| P2 (after narrowing) → P3 | Defect criteria must first be written in red (2.4.1/2.4.3) and the multi-file corpus layer (2.3.2) must exist so that red tests have somewhere to run                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| P3 → P4                   | Fix bugs before refactoring; the reverse order causes bugs to be固化 into the stage table as “established behavior”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| P3.5 → P4                 | RFC-029g's (#399) deletion surface covers the rewrite targets of P4 4.2.2 / P5 / P6 / P7 / P8 (the list is in §P3.5 of this document)—the reverse order means repeating the same deletions on the new grammar, checker layout, and IR (D56)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| P4 → P5                   | The `include!` refactor and checker split modify the same file                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| P5 → P6                   | Consecutive changes to the same file must be separated, otherwise regressions cannot be bisected                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| P6 → P7 / P8              | If type representations do not converge first, the new IR grows into a third representation; **P7 gate = the exits of phases A/B/C in 6.9** (I1–I3, I5, I7; that is, 6.9.2 including C3, 6.9.3 including d, and completed 6.9.4), while D (Σ) does not block; P7 may consume the quantifier-derived views and defeq interface but must not create a parallel ledger; the 7.0 pure-move batch is a P7 prerequisite and is not subject to this gate, but it must not consume an undecided defeq / quantifier interface |
| P7/P8 → P9                | The 9.5 snapshot baseline and the 9.3 `pub(crate)` leak count reach their final form only after P7/P8                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

### Parallelizable Groups

| Group                                    | Members                                                                               | Basis                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **A (the only group authorized by RFC)** | P7 ∥ P8                                                                               | The file sets are disjoint: `ir.rs`/`ir_gen.rs`/`bytecode.rs`/`translator.rs` vs `lexer/*`/`parser/*`                                                                                                                                                                |
| B                                        | 1.2.1 ∥ 1.2.2 ∥ 1.2.3 ∥ 1.2.4                                                         | Each independently adds `mod` and can be reverted per file                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| C                                        | 2.1 ∥ 2.2 ∥ 2.3.1 ∥ 2.3.2 ∥ 2.4                                                       | The three layers of criteria are independent of one another                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| D                                        | 4.4 (proof-layer wrap-up) ∥ the entire P6 line                                        | `02` explicitly states in S5 that it “should proceed independently of S1-S4”                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| E                                        | 4.2.5 ∥ 4.2.6 ∥ 4.2.8                                                                 | All are independent after 4.1 is complete                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| F                                        | 9.3 ∥ 9.9 ∥ 9.10 (the three scripts introduced under P0 may be developed in parallel) | The 9.5 snapshot baseline must be taken last                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| G                                        | S3 ∥ S4 ∥ S5                                                                          | The file sets are disjoint (verified 2026-10-05: S3 modifies `docs/src/dev/design/check/` + `config.js`; S4 modifies `docs/src/rfc/` + the `check_tracking.py` generator; S5 modifies two `pub` locations under `src/frontend/core/typecheck/`; no pairwise overlap) |

**Cannot run in parallel (file overlap)**: P1(1.1.x) ∥ P8(8.0.x); 1.2.1 ∥ 8.3.2; 6.0 ∥ S2 (B6/E5 in
the same batch of files); 4.3.2 ∥ 9.2 (already unified under P4); **3.4 ∥ P3.5** (`checker.rs` /
`environment.rs` are the same files—the external track's pub-deletion batch and the silent-channel
fixes must be serialized).

**New internal documentation constraints**: 6.0→6.1→6.2→6.3→6.4→6.5→6.6 is strictly serial; 7.0 →
7a→7b→7c→7d is strictly serial (7.0 is the pure-move prerequisite for P7), and 7b's `Phi` arm must
precede 7d.

## Key Decisions and Rationale

- **P0 is an independent phase rather than part of P9**—gates are “post-hoc checks,” while rules are
  “pre-hoc judgments.” P9's scripts cannot prevent “patching when a refactor was required”; only
  D0–D4's review checklist can.
- **P9 as the sole authoritative list of CI scripts**—the three concurrent lists underlying gap G3
  made closure impossible. This table merges them so that the 10 active scripts each belong to
  exactly one phase (9.8 was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24), with report-only status and
  hard-failure timing explicitly traceable.
- **P3.5 incorporates RFC-029g rather than leaving it as an “independent track to do after the
  refactor”**—its deletion surface overlaps with the rewrite surfaces of P4/P5/P6/P7/P8 (RFC-039
  D56). Deferring it until after the refactor means repeating the same deletions on the new grammar,
  checker layout, and IR; this is the same lesson as incorporating `2315`/`2341` into 7e and RFC
  status correction into S4.
- **P5's steps are supplied by this document rather than merged into P4**—P4 is already the largest
  single-point risk, and adding the checker split would exceed a revertible granularity.
- **5.3.2 uses “zero caller changes” as its hard acceptance criterion**—the split must be
  independently revertable.

## Known Limitations and Risks

- **1.3.x (fix the exposed defects) has no regression criterion**—it only says “the fixed defects
  must not be rolled back,” without requiring a record of “what was fixed.” **Execution
  convention**: every 1.3.x fix commit message must reference the fixed test name and defect
  description as a basis for subsequent binary attribution.
- ~~**7b.1 is too coarse a granularity**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: split into 7b.1a / 7b.1b as two
  exclusive commits under DoD 6.
- **8.2.1 is too coarse a granularity**—about 89 renamed references; a missed change **silently
  changes associativity**.
- ~~**D17 / D20 have no corresponding third-level tasks**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: D17 landed as
  7e.1, and D20 landed as 4.5.1/4.5.2; D32/D34 opcode reclamation was incorporated into 7e.1, with
  the deletion action remaining in P10 S6.
- ~~**The `2315` / `2341` data-loss defects were originally assigned to “separate issues”**~~
  **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: incorporated as 7e.2 / 7e.3. The exception table (throw/try) is core
  language semantics and must not be left for future implementation.
- ~~**E2 (`lib.rs:568/582` `todo!()`) has no phase ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**:
  incorporated into P10 S2.
- ~~**F7 (opcode gate extractor) has ambiguous ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: incorporated
  into the generation-time gate task under P10 S6.

## Conflict Registry: All Adjudicated

> **The original “Conflict Registry” C1–C8 and the open questions in each document have all
> converged into the [RFC-039 Decision Registry](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md)
> (D1–D50).** This document retains no pending items. The mapping is:

| Original ID | Issue                                                                          | Decision                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| C1          | `precedence_inline.rs` is resurrected under P1 and deleted under P8            | **Resurrect** (the P1 prerequisite is a test with real assertions); P8 no longer deletes the file (Pratt is retained)                                                            |
| C2          | “Grammar-driven” commitment vs table-based implementation                      | **Fallback approach**: retain Pratt + a single declarative precedence table + source-aligned cross-checking of the two `BinOp` sets (the LALRPOP route is withdrawn); see P8 8.3 |
| C3          | Conflict between the C6 category definition and S1 classification              | **S1 belongs to C6** (resurrection requires no equivalence criterion, only regression tests); the C6 definition is expanded to “pure deletion or pure resurrection”              |
| C4          | `test_release_plan_spans_consumed` allowlist                                   | **No allowlist**; the difference must be empty; if it cannot be empty, the `ReleasePlan` contract is defective → change it to `PlanId` (D20/D41)                                 |
| C5          | Internal differences between the two `Aggregation` functions remain unverified | **P4's 4.2.7 has made it a required verification item**, to be confirmed line by line during implementation                                                                      |
| C6          | The wasm playground fix requires P4's `ProgramKind`                            | **Merge the wasm-path defect fix into 4.2.8**; P3 handles only the three native entry points                                                                                     |
| C7          | Ownership of `method_def_ordinals`                                             | **Assign to 04** (P7 batch c), see D21                                                                                                                                           |
| C8          | `upvalue_count` correction and the `.42` version number                        | **Fix it + change `VERSION` from 4 to 5** (the format header already has `MAGIC` + `VERSION` fields, `codegen/bytecode.rs:14-16`), see D17                                       |
